title: Base change for open-closed immersions
statement:
Let $j:U\to X$ be both an open and a closed immersion of schemes
and let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism, forming the
cartesian square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
Y\times_XU&\xrightarrow{\;h\;}&Y\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle p}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle g}\\
U&\xrightarrow{\;j\;}&X .
\end{array}
$$

Then for every abelian sheaf $F$ on $U_{\Et}$ the base change map
$g^{-1}j_*F\to h_*p^{-1}F$ of
[def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] is an isomorphism.

proof.text: A closed immersion is finite, by Mathlib's IsFinite.instOfIsClosedImmersion. Apply this to j, using [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The open-immersion hypothesis is not needed for this specialization.
The chosen identification in [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] and its projection equations give IsPullback p h j g by CategoryTheory.IsPullback.of_iso_pullback.

Apply the underived part of [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange], namely AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.isIso_baseChangeMap_of_isFinite, with coefficient category AddCommGrpCat and the pullback square from step 2. This proves invertibility of the specified natural transformation baseChangeMap, and hence of its component at F. All coefficient-category assumptions are supplied by the existing abelian-group and small-etale-site instances. No nonemptiness assumption is used, so empty schemes and the identity immersion are included.

proof_origin.place: isIso_baseChangeMap_of_isFinite, specialized to the finite morphism j; AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.instOfIsClosedImmersion in Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Finite.lean and CategoryTheory.IsPullback.of_iso_pullback supply the hypotheses. D4, 2026-10-20: shorter route using an existing proved tool; the unit has no realized steps bypassed by this specialization.
